newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Troubled Sabena has 2 bln Bfr H1 1996 loss.
newsitem.headline: Troubled Sabena has 2 bln Bfr H1 1996 loss.

text.p: Belgian national airline Sabena, 49.5-percent owned by Swissair, said it had a two billion Belgian franc consolidated net loss in the first half of 1996.
"We had about two billion less (in earnings) than budgetted...the loss will be two billion," a spokesman said late on Wednesday.
He added that the second half of the year would be better but that the disappointing first-half earnings made the carrier's proposed key restructuring plan -- "Horizon 1998" -- more urgent.
Sabena's chief executive Paul Reutlinger said in June he wanted Sabena to be profitable again from 1998 and to achieve this by finding extra savings of 4.7 billion Belgian francs.

Swissair said in August its first half loss narrowed to 51 million Swiss francs from a 86 million Swiss franc deficit last year but blamed Sabena for a large part of a 27 million Swiss franc loss at Swissair's associated companies.
Sabena is currently holding crucial talks with trade unions aimed at bringing the company back to profit.

The two reached initial agreement on a first series of measures last month, including early retirement at 52 years of age, voluntary redundancies, part-time work, holidays without pay and internal transfers. A final deal is due to be hammered out by the end of this month.
Sabena had a 1995 group loss before provisions of 530 million francs compared with a 1.23 billion franc loss in 1994.

Reutlinger said in June that Sabena's 1996 earnings to May had been lagging company expectations due to a series of strikes in February which led to the resignation of Sabena's Belgian chief executive and chairman Pierre Godfroid.
Sabena denied airline sector rumours that Sabena and Virgin Express, the regional airline of British entrepreneur Richard Branson, had reached agreement on flights to London.
Sources said Sabena would give up to Virgin Express its nine daily flights to London if Virgin agreed not to fly to the Swiss city of Geneva.
Several pilots said Virgin Express, launched in April after Branson bought 90 percent of EuroBelgian Airlines SA (EBA), was currently recruiting crews for flights to London.
Virgin Express chief executive Jonathan Ornstein declined to comment on the rumours.

Reutlinger, marketing manager at Swissair before moving to Sabena, was named chairman of the board of 80-percent owned regional transport subsidiary Delta Air Transport (DAT) on Wednesday, succeeding Bernadette Franzi-van Milders who left the company last month.
DAT decided last year to renew its entire fleet with 23 Avro RJ85 jets from British Aerospace
